title: Cast Iron vs PVC in Drainage Systems
description: Selecting the right material for drainage, waste, and vent (DWV) systems requires balancing acoustic performance, fire rating, and ease of installation. Heavy cast iron piping excels at absorbing fluid flow noise in multi-story residential vertical stacks, making living spaces much quieter. In contrast, Schedule 40 PVC is lightweight, cost-effective, highly resistant to chemical corrosion, and easily joined with solvent welding. However, PVC transmits more sound and requires dedicated fire-stopping assemblies when penetrating rated walls or floors. Always consult local building codes and project specifications when selecting DWV materials.
